thesis: Macro conditions are mixed but restrictive for a small-cap long-duration growth company. The Fed raised the policy range to 3.75%-4.00%, the 10-year real Treasury yield was 2.61% on Sep. 17, and inflation remained above target, increasing discount-rate and equity-duration pressure. Against that, the NFCI stayed looser than average and corporate credit spreads remained tight, so there is no broad financing stress. Recommend risk_budget_multiplier 0.80: preserve Moonshot optionality but pace entries more slowly than a large-cap self-funded compounder.

evidence.claim: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00% on Sep. 16 and said inflation remained elevated.
The 10-year real Treasury yield was 2.61% on Sep. 17, a high real discount-rate backdrop for long-duration equities.
evidence.source: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Real Yield Curve Rates

evidence.claim: The Chicago Fed NFCI was -0.560 for the week ending Sep. 11; negative values indicate looser-than-average financial conditions.
evidence.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago / FRED NFCI

evidence.claim: Investment-grade corporate OAS was 0.78% and high-yield OAS 2.70% on Sep. 16, indicating no broad credit-market stress.
August CPI rose 3.4% year over year and core CPI 2.4%, leaving headline inflation above the Fed's 2% target.
evidence.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI, August 2026

evidence.claim: Q2 real GDP grew 1.5% annualized while real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.2%, showing resilient private demand despite softer headline growth.
evidence.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP second estimate, Q2 2026

counterevidence: Credit spreads are tight and the NFCI remains negative, so capital markets are not signaling systemic stress.
Private domestic demand remains resilient, reducing near-term recession risk.
PL has substantial liquidity and positive H1 FCF, making it less exposed to immediate refinancing stress than a typical pre-revenue small-cap.
Core CPI at 2.4% is closer to target than headline inflation, leaving scope for policy pressure to ease if disinflation resumes.
unknowns: Whether the September hike is followed by additional tightening in 2026.
Whether real yields stay above 2.5% or mean-revert after policy repricing.
Whether equity issuance conditions for high-beta small caps remain as receptive if volatility rises.
Whether geopolitical and government-budget developments alter sovereign Earth-observation spending.
falsifiers: 10-year real yields fall materially while inflation cools and credit spreads stay tight, supporting a higher multiplier.
NFCI turns positive and IG/HY spreads widen sharply, requiring a lower risk budget.
Small-cap equity issuance conditions materially improve while PL becomes more self-funded, reducing macro sensitivity.

key_kpis.name: 10-year real Treasury yield
key_kpis.threshold: Below ~2.25% would reduce duration pressure; sustained >2.75% would justify more caution

key_kpis.name: NFCI / credit spreads
key_kpis.threshold: Negative NFCI and contained spreads support access to capital; sharp widening signals stress

key_kpis.name: Policy/inflation path
key_kpis.threshold: Disinflation without further hikes supports a larger risk budget

next_checks: Next FOMC communication and policy-rate path
September/October inflation releases and real-yield trend
NFCI, HY spreads and small-cap financing conditions
